name: @swampratnz/agent-base
description: Community-agnostic base framework for Claude Agent SDK bots: platform adapters, RBAC, persistent memory, confirm-gated tools, and a module API for building specific agents on top.
_comment_exports: Node's exports map is an ALLOW-LIST: a subpath with no entry fails resolution with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, and TypeScript reports the same gap as TS2307. The `.` barrel is a ~15-symbol convenience surface (createAgent, migrate, the schema manifest); a real module imports the tree directly — community-agent alone imports 53 modules — so the two wildcards below export every compiled module with its types. `./*.js` is the form to write, matching this repo's own `.js`-suffixed internal specifiers (`@swampratnz/agent-base/router.js`); `./*` accepts the extensionless form as well, and Node prefers the longer suffix pattern, so `router.js` never resolves through `./*` to `dist/router.js.js`. Wildcards rather than 53 hand-written entries because an enumeration silently omits every module added after it was written — the failure mode being fixed here. This does mean the whole of `dist/` is public API surface: that is the intent of a framework consumed by composition, and `files` already decides what `dist/` contains.
_comment_exports_default: Conditions are matched in declaration order, so `default` is the catch-all that must come LAST. It exists because the map was `{types, import}` only, which makes every condition other than `import` — `require` above all — fail with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: a resolution error that says the subpath is not exported, when the truth is that it is exported and only ESM-shaped. `default` and not `require` on purpose. A `require` key is a promise of a CommonJS artifact; this package is `"type": "module"` and ships none, and pointing `require` at an ESM file would state something false in the one place a bundler trusts most. `default` states what is actually true — one artifact, offered under every condition — and lets the loader decide. On the Node this package supports (`engines: >=22`, and require(ESM) is unflagged from 22.12) a `require()` of these paths now resolves and works; on an older loader it fails as ERR_REQUIRE_ESM, which names the real constraint instead of misdirecting to the exports map. Found via swampratnz/agent-base#11, from community-agent#960 where `createRequire().resolve()` hit exactly this.
_comment_files: An allowlist, so anything not named here is absent from the tarball. `dist` has to carry the storage/schema/*.sql fragments as well as the JS — the build script copies them and check-dist-schema.mjs fails the build if it did not, because a consumer that installs this and cannot `migrate:prod` is broken. `scripts` ships the two gate scripts a scaffolded repo runs out of node_modules (see template/package.json). npm always adds README.md, LICENSE and package.json regardless of this list. Verify with `npm pack --dry-run` after changing it.

scripts._comment_prepublishOnly: Runs on `npm publish` (not on `npm pack`/`npm ci`), so a hand-run publish from a laptop can never ship a stale or missing dist/. The publish workflow builds first anyway — this is the backstop for the path that skips it.
scripts.build: tsc -p tsconfig.json && node scripts/copy-schema.mjs && node scripts/check-dist-schema.mjs

_comment_publishConfig: Public npmjs.com, NOT GitHub Packages — see docs/ROADMAP.md's Phase 0 decisions. GitHub Packages' npm registry demands a token even to INSTALL a public package, which would put an auth step between the production deploy host and a redeploy; public npm needs none. The registry is pinned here rather than left to whatever .npmrc the publishing machine happens to have.
_comment_baileys_peer: Baileys is an OPTIONAL PEER, not a dependency, and that is deliberate. @whiskeysockets/baileys declares libsignal over git+https, and npm 12 refuses every git-protocol fetch (EALLOWGIT) — so while it sat in dependencies, NOBODY on npm 12 could install this framework, whether or not they wanted WhatsApp, because npm resolves the whole tree before anything runs. As an optional peer the constraint follows the FEATURE instead of the framework: a Discord-only agent installs on any npm, and a Baileys deployment adds @whiskeysockets/baileys to its own dependencies and is unchanged. The runtime import is confined to src/platforms/whatsapp/baileysAdapter.ts — wire.ts uses "import type", which erases — so a consumer that never imports that module never needs the package, and one that imports it without installing baileys gets ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, which is honest. It stays in devDependencies because THIS repo builds and tests the adapter. See issue #29.
